newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power mostly stable despite cold.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power mostly stable despite cold.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Southeast were mostly steady Wednesday, despite forecasts calling for much colder temperatures Friday.
"Everyone is just waiting for the cold to arrive. Prices will probably move higher tomorrow," one market source said.

Temperatures in the Southeast are expected to remain below-normal through Thursday but then fall to 10-22 degrees F below normal Friday. Weather Services Corp's six- to 10-day outlook is calling for more below-normal temperatures.

Firm, peak power prices into the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) territory for Thursday were in the $26.00-28.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) area, as compared with Tuesday's tighter range of $26.00-27.00.
Firm, peak power moving out of TVA was carrying a premium in the $28.00-31.00 per MWh range, traders said.
Firm, off-peak electricity prices into TVA for Thursday were still assessed at $16.00.
At the Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak electricity prices in 16 hour blocks for Thursday delivery also held steady in the $26.00-27.00 range.
Firm, off-peak power for Thursday at the Ga./Fla. border was notionally flat in a range of $18.00-21.00.
Despite the lack of movement in electricity prices, spot natural gas prices were up sharply in the $4.20s and $4.30s per million British thermal units along the Gulf Coast.

Separately, the City of Lakeland, Fla., reported that a 90 megawatt power unit, fueled by natural gas and fuel oil, would restart sometime Thursday and be back on-line this weekend after shutting down in October.
